To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

usability benefits are supported by a range of architectural tactics, that these tactics can be organized in a hierarchy of increasing complexity, and that this hierarchy of architectural complexity is related to the complexity of usability benefits.

1) there are 27 general scenarios that can be applied to any system; 2) these scenarios can be organized into an emergent usability hierarchy; 3) each scenario can be linked to a set of architectural tactics and to one or more architectural patterns; 4) these architectural patterns can be used to proactively support usability; 5) the usability hierarchy is a useful tool to guide software architecture design and to identify usability problems early in the life of a system;

1) usability is a quality attribute of software that can be addressed by the architectural design of a software system; 2) usability is a complex quality attribute, and it is difficult to achieve; and 3) the usability of a system is improved by the use of a variety of architectural design tactics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between software architecture and usability, and the impact that architecture has on usability.
identifying the architectural patterns that support usability and linking usability to architecture.
the question: "What are the usability benefits of architectural design decisions?"
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

usability benefits are best served through an architectural approach that is iterative and incremental, that uses a variety of architectural patterns, and that is informed by a comprehensive set of usability scenarios.
usability is an important quality to be addressed during software design and that architectural patterns can support the achievement of many usability goals.

the usability benefits that are supported through architectural patterns are: 1) the user's perception of the system as a whole is improved; 2) the user is more likely to use the system; 3) the user is likely to use the correct functionality; 4) the user is able to complete the desired task; and 5) the user is less likely to make errors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a framework for linking usability and architectural patterns, and that we provide a set of scenarios and a set of architectural patterns to support the framework.
usability benefits are linked to architectural patterns and these links are discoverable early in the software development life-cycle.
we have identified a variety of architectural patterns that support the achievement of a wide variety of potential usability benefits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the architectural tactics that support usability are not limited to separation of the interface from the system's functionality.
usability can be linked directly to software architectural design and can be addressed proactively.
there is a direct link between the scenarios that a system supports and the usability benefits that the system can provide.
